claims.assertion: Yazhi describes intersecting timelines where different histories can converge on the same event; a lie remains false rather than automatically being true in another line.
claims.speaker: Yazhi
claims.qualifiers: She presents this as her model of historical interpretation.

claims.assertion: Yazhi says time has no fixed direction; consciousness animates perceived event sequences, and each observer experiences only part of the whole.
claims.speaker: Yazhi
claims.qualifiers: She treats linear chronology and dimensional labels as explanatory conventions.
